Subject: High 5xx/429 spike since 06/18 morning — production impact

Karthik,

We observed a sustained spike in 5xx and 429 responses starting ~08:40 PDT this morning for our production tenant (ember-prod). Throughput dropped suddenly and many of our upstream workers started retrying aggressively which amplified the issue. We're seeing timeouts and end-user latency > 3s on token-heavy requests; incident affecting multiple regions.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on your side? We need an immediate remediation plan and an estimate for customer credits for the impacted window. Attaching a short error sample.

Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream
Approx impact window: 2026-06-18T08:40:00-2026-06-18T11:05:00 PDT

Please loop in engineering and CS — this is causing customer complaints.

Thanks,
Sam

Sam/Team — I set up a 30-min bridge for 09:50 PDT (details in calendar invite). High-level mitigation options we've started:

- Temporary throttling of client retries at our gateway to reduce retry storm amplification.
- Route Ember traffic to a warmed pool/region that has spare capacity to reduce 429s while we stabilize autoscaler config.
- Toggle stricter per-tenant token limits for requests over 2k tokens to reduce tail latency.

We'll push a configuration change for gateway retry handling in the next 20–30 minutes and monitor. I'll upload a short remediation plan after the call.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samuel Park <samuel.park@embertech.com>, Clara Liu <clara.liu@embertech.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:16:00-07:00
Subject: Root cause & immediate fixes (summary)

Team — quick summary after digging into metrics and logs:

- Root cause: a recent autoscaler rollout (v2.3.7) had a regression in the cold-start detection thresholds for certain model variants used by Ember. When provisioning lagged, clients continued retrying; combined with sticky client routing this created concentrated load on a subset of serving nodes.
- Result: increased queue depths => timeouts and HTTP 5xx (backend failures) and 429 (rate limiting) as nodes hit concurrency limits.
- Retry amplification: many client SDKs retried with exponential backoff disabled in a few workflows, which amplified peak load.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
1) Reverted autoscaler rollout for ember-prod to v2.3.6 (completed 10:05 PDT).
2) Applied gateway-level retry dampening (slow-start window + jitter).
3) Brought up warmed instances in us-west-2 to absorb burst traffic.

Preliminary impact: error rates dropped ~85% within 40 minutes of mitigation; full normalization by 11:00 PDT. I'm attaching the error log bundle and a short timeline.

Attachment: error-logs-ember-20260618.zip

I'll prepare a formal post-mortem and a proposed set of code/config safeguards to prevent recurrence.

-David
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
